historical_reviews.v3_1: Scopes evidence to one LDAP-associated certificate object; it does not borrow AD coverage or claim a successful bind, TLS negotiation or active trust decision.

original_test_intent: Retrieve one Redfish certificate identified under AccountService LDAP and confirm the response is readable and error-free.
original_method: Discover an actual member of the LDAP Certificates collection, perform one authenticated GET over trusted TLS and validate the public certificate representation without changing LDAP or certificate configuration.
manual_activity: Provide the firmware-advertised LDAP Certificates link, approved read-only access package and policy for retaining certificate and directory identity fields.
required_inputs: LDAP service and Certificates collection links
CertificateId proven to be a collection member
safety_requirements: Never embed credentials or bypass TLS without an approved exception
Query one advertised LDAP certificate member only
Never request or retain private keys or passwords
Do not create, renew, replace or delete certificates
Do not enable, disable or reconfigure LDAP
Redact sensitive directory and certificate identity
Do not equate metadata retrieval with LDAP bind or LDAPS trust success
agent_execution_scope: Record BMC, firmware and AccountService identity
Read LDAP and its Certificates collection
Select and validate one member URI
Send one GET and capture status
Validate JSON, schema, resource identity, fingerprint and exposed validity fields
Record absence of actions and mutations

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The endpoint fits the LDAP certificate item, but free-form CERT_ID, `-k`, credential exposure and full-output retention omit essential identity and confidentiality controls.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Follow the advertised LDAP Certificates link, choose a returned member, and issue one verified-TLS GET with secret-backed credentials while validating status, schema, member identity, public fingerprint and redaction.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The LDAP certificate resource and 15/10 timing are preserved; no certificate role, issuer, hostname or bind expectation is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use collection discovery to bind the requested object to LDAP before collecting a small, validated and redacted certificate evidence set.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces fixed-path trust and insecure full dumps with advertised-link discovery, verified transport, status/schema/fingerprint checks and data-minimized evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers one LDAP certificate resource. It does not exercise user bind, server reachability, certificate-chain selection or LDAP authorization.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A readable object can be stale, unused or unrelated to a successful LDAP session; schema and field availability also vary by firmware.

project_override_considerations: If the firmware distinguishes generic LDAP from ActiveDirectory, require the certificate member to originate from the LDAP object specifically. Missing certificate bytes must be reported as a schema limitation rather than bypassed through secret-bearing endpoints.
expected_evidence: Advertised LDAP Certificates collection and selected member URI
Public certificate fingerprint and validity metadata when exposed
No LDAP/certificate action or state change

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item, GET path, criteria and script all concern a single LDAP certificate resource. Security and acceptance details are incomplete but the sources do not disagree about the operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: All missing elements are standard read-only access, schema and evidence-governance inputs rather than an unresolved engineering definition.

review_improvement: Makes LDAP collection membership part of identity, protects transport and credentials, minimizes certificate evidence and prevents a read-only object query from being overclaimed as operational directory trust.
independent_technical_reasoning: The path namespace matters: an LDAP certificate and an ActiveDirectory certificate may have similar schemas yet belong to different service configurations, so an ID copied from the adjacent AD collection is not acceptable. The collection link and member URI form the identity chain for this case. A public-certificate fingerprint can establish which object was read, but neither a 200 response nor a valid date range shows that the BMC selected it in an LDAPS handshake or completed an LDAP bind. Evidence therefore remains resource-centric, redacted and explicitly non-operational.
